text:
maya: Heads up — saw a batch of GPU inference pods land on cpu nodes this morning and latency jumped. cluster-autoscaler didn't spin up any gpu nodes :thinking:

raj: ugh. any failures in scheduler events?

maya: kubectl describe showed: 
`0/12 nodes are available: 8 node(s) had taint {gpu:true:NoSchedule}, 4 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector`. The pod spec includes nodeSelector: {accelerator: nvidia} and tolerations are present on the app container, but the logging sidecar seems to be missing tolerations.

tess: sidecar missing toleration will prevent the pod from being scheduled onto tainted gpu nodes unless toleration is on the pod level (all containers share pod tolerations). Is this a per-container thing?

kevin: pods only support tolerations at pod level, but some build tooling was accidentally setting tolerations only in the app container annotation and our webhook didn't copy it to the pod metadata.

natalie: infra-bot showed autoscaler ignored the pod: `pod has unschedulable nodeSelector` in the logs. If webhook set nodeSelector that doesn't match any nodegroup labels, CA won't scale.

maya: attaching the minimal repro pod YAML we used (redacted):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-test
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    accelerator: nvidia
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: infra/gpu-app
  - name: logger
    image: infra/logger
```

raj: yep. two issues: (1) our mutating webhook sometimes writes nodeSelector onto pod.spec but doesn't merge tolerations from the template; (2) logger DaemonSet has a podSecurityContext that removes tolerations via a copy step.

tess: quickfix: add pod-level toleration to the webhook patch and redeploy webhook. toleration snippet: 
```yaml
 tolerations:
 - key: "gpu"
   operator: "Equal"
   value: "true"
   effect: "NoSchedule"
```

kevin: also consider using nodeAffinity preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution instead of hard nodeSelector where possible — CA can scale nodegroups when affinity requests resources, but hard nodeSelector that references a label not present on any ASG will block scale up.

maya: infra-bot logs suggest this happened right after last release of our sidecar image (2026-02-05). Probably webhook changes in that release.

natalie: proposed action items:
- roll back webhook patch to v3.1.2 (quick)
- add unit test verifying pod-level tolerations don't get dropped (medium)
- audit DaemonSet for any mutating initcontainers that rewrite pod metadata (high)
- add e2e that simulates tainted gpu node + autoscaler scale up (medium)

raj: I'll open the PR to patch webhook and add the test. grabbing ownership of rollback if needed.

tess: I'll check the logger DaemonSet and daemonset image diff. If it rewrites metadata we should stop that behavior.

kevin: one more note — when CA doesn't scale, check cluster-autoscaler logs for: `no template for nodeGroup matching labels` and `Skipping because node selectors mismatch` — saved us debugging earlier.

maya: thanks all. if we revert quickly we should see GPU nodes come up and pods reschedule. tagging infra-oncall to watch for any residual evictions :eyes:

infra-bot: Incident watcher created: #INC-2026-0427 — gpu-scheduling-regression. Assigned to eng-infra.

natalie: I'll follow up with a short postmortem once we close the rollback and tests.

maya: also want a short note in runbook: how to triage taint/toleration + CA problems (kubectl describe pod, kubectl get nodes --show-labels, ca logs location).

raj: added to my PR checklist. PR incoming in ~30m. :rocket:
